Dana — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. I appreciate the context. Short answer: the asks as written (direct escrow + cash refunds + broad termination for two months) are outside Redwood's standard commercial model.

Longer answer and immediate next steps:
- Our baseline approach is service credits for SLA misses, with termination only in the case of pervasive, repeated failures that we define with clear thresholds and cure periods.
- We can consider a limited, negotiable escrow (an agreed-upon deposit tied to the first year of committed fees) for strategic enterprise commitments, but it would need to be structured and capped.
- Liquidated damages are a hard no for us in the generic form you propose — we typically offer a damages cap tied to a multiple of monthly fees (not open-ended) and prefer credit remedies because they directly offset customer impact.

I'll loop Legal (Marissa) and Contracts (Priyom) to propose a concrete counter that preserves your CFO's need for economic protection while limiting Redwood's open liability. Expect a proposal by COB Monday.

Jonas / Priyom — forwarding Dana's redlines. Quick thoughts:

- Accepting an escrow tied to performance is possible for a strategic account, but we should limit to a single-year deposit equal to 1–3 months of committed fees and require that NovaCorp first exhaust credits before any cash drawdown.
- Termination for two months in a 12-mo window is too permissive. Recommend: termination right only after two "severe" events as defined below AND after a 30-day cure period, with the cap on damages set at 6 months of fees.
- Liquidated damages clauses are risky from a legal perspective (opens high exposure). If they insist, cap at 3 months and require they pursue credits first; otherwise allow termination + refund of any unused prepaid fees.

Suggested language to propose:
1) Performance Escrow: Upon execution, Redwood will place a refundable escrow equal to 2 months of the committed annual fees in an escrow account governed by a third-party escrow agent. Funds may only be disbursed upon demonstrable failure to cure a "severe" SLA breach within the cure period and only after customer has accepted service credits for the period in question.
2) Termination Right: Customer may terminate for cause only after two (2) separate "severe" SLA breaches in a rolling 12-month period, each defined as (a) monthly availability <97.5% OR (b) p50 latency >2x baseline for >=48 consecutive hours. Either event triggers a 30-day cure window. If Redwood fails to cure, Customer may terminate and receive a pro-rated refund of pre-paid fees.
3) Damage Cap: Any cash compensation (including escrow draw or refunds) limited to six (6) months of committed fees.

I think this gives them economic protection while keeping our liability bounded. Priyom — any procurement escalation (discounts/credits) we want to layer on top?

Marissa
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference

Dana — thanks for your patience. Attached is a consolidated counter (see summary bullets below; full redline attached for your counsel). I tried to balance NovaCorp's need for an economic remedy with limits on Redwood's open liability.

Summary of Redwood counterproposal:
- Performance Escrow: Redwood will place an escrow equal to 2 months of the first-year committed fees with a neutral escrow agent. Escrow draw only after (a) a documented "severe" SLA breach, (b) a 30-day cure window, and (c) a joint postmortem that confirms failure to remediate.
- Termination: Customer may terminate for cause after two (2) separate "severe" SLA breaches in a rolling 12-month period. Termination entitles Customer to a pro-rated refund of any unused pre-paid fees; termination does not automatically trigger additional liquidated damages beyond the escrow/refund cap.
- Damage Cap: Total cash remedies (escrow + refund) capped at six (6) months of committed fees.
- Latency: Latency-based remedies tied to p50/p95 deltas against an agreed baseline traffic profile and require 48 consecutive hours of sustained regression.
- Credits & Commercial Concession: Redwood will provide a one-time implementation credit equal to 10% of the first-month invoice if NovaCorp accepts the above language.

We also require the contract to include standard exclusions and a joint monitoring/alerting feed for the first 90 days post-go-live so we can proactively address issues.

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Counter_NovaCorp_redline.pdf (inline in this thread).

If this is acceptable in principle, please let me know and we can route through your counsel and ours for final redlines + DocuSign. If you need tighter cash remedies, we'll need an approvals route through VP Product / CFO (this will likely require additional commercial offset).
